official.description_text:
Postdoc in cellulose feedstocks and small-scale nitration
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health
Job description
Would you like to build the scientific foundation for Swedish nitrocellulose? We are looking for a postdoc at the competence centre Svenskt Krut at KTH, where academia, government agencies and industry jointly strengthen Sweden's capability in nitrocellulose (NC).
In the project we map how the properties of the cellulose feedstock affect the nitrocellulose that can be produced. Your role is to characterise different cellulose feedstocks – including fibre structure, crystallinity, purity, accessibility and water retention – and relate these parameters to the suitability of the raw materials.
You will plan and carry out systematic small-scale nitration trials under controlled and safe conditions, analyse the resulting NC with the centre's analysis package and quantify the relationship between feedstock and NC properties. The work is carried out at the Department of Fibre and Polymer Technology and in close collaboration with FOI, including at least one longer stay there.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Documented scientific expertise in cellulose, fibre or polymer chemistry, demonstrated through publications.
Experience of characterising cellulose or fibrous materials, e.g. structure, crystallinity and purity.
Very good command of English, spoken and written, as it is required in the daily work.
As a person you are independent, take initiative and have a strong ability to collaborate in an interdisciplinary environment.
Swedish citizenship.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience of experimental synthesis or process work under explicit safety requirements.
Experience of design of experiments and of linking feedstock parameters to product properties.
Teaching abilities.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: Postdoc position in cellulose feedstock characterisation and small-scale nitration trials at KTH's Svenskt Krut competence centre, focusing on mapping how feedstock properties affect nitrocellulose production. Work involves systematic experimental design, material characterisation, and cross-institutional collaboration with government and industry partners.

thematic_fit.rationale: The researcher's expertise is in human-centred XR, collaborative immersive systems, and spatial learning. This position is pure materials chemistry (cellulose, nitration, polymer characterisation) with no connection to HCI, immersive systems, spatial cognition, learning, or user evaluation. The mention of 'small-scale trials' and 'experimental design' does not bridge the domain gap.

methodological_fit.rationale: Both involve experimental design and structured trials. However, the researcher's experimental methodology is grounded in human-subjects research, user studies, and spatial performance measurement. This position requires chemistry lab protocols, material characterisation methods, and analytical chemistry—entirely different methodological foundations. No transferable skills align.

growth_value.rationale: This position would not advance the researcher's stated capability gaps or target identity. It introduces chemistry and materials science expertise orthogonal to HCI, immersive systems, or spatial cognition. Does not build toward doctoral research in human-centred XR or collaborative immersive systems.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong institution, but the Department of Fibre and Polymer Technology does not align with HCI or immersive systems research. The researcher's priority institutions (Aalto, TU Delft) and target groups work in design, HCI, and immersive learning—not materials chemistry. No pathway to the researcher's target identity.

eligibility_flags: Requires completed PhD by employment start (1 October 2026); researcher has MSc in progress and thesis stage—does not meet doctoral degree requirement at time of application.
Swedish citizenship requirement stated as mandatory ('Krav' in Swedish). Researcher profile does not specify citizenship status.
risks: Fundamental domain mismatch: materials chemistry vs. human-centred XR.
Does not satisfy doctoral degree requirement at application deadline.
Possible security clearance requirement (Protective Security Act) may complicate non-Swedish nationals.
Postdoc position assumes completed PhD; researcher is still in thesis stage.
